patch.value: Expose a monotonic history fence for native conditional SDK updates

The new preview/CAS rule requires an under-lock monotonically growing witness. SDK 2026.10.24 BulkItemUpdateMutation exposes only match: BulkItemUniqueKey (key/value), with no expectedHistoryHead or expectedHistoryLength precondition on native lifecycle updates. A real non-git SDK probe freezes Date to the inspected updated_at, performs title Initial -> Foreign -> Initial, then commits an update matched to the old timestamp: history grows 1 -> 4, timestamp stays equal, conflict is false and stale Planned wins. This is an SDK timestamp-match limitation, not a field-presence regression. Searched public SDK declarations for transaction, match, history and preconditions, and open upstream issue searches history head precondition and ABA match returned zero. Desired API: BulkItemUpdateMutation.expectedHistoryHead or an equivalent monotonic native lifecycle precondition checked under the existing mutation lock; terminal close must carry the same contract. BeforeMutationHook exists, but using a package-defined history/CAS policy would reimplement SDK concurrency behavior and needs a shared upstream design. Orchestrator should report upstream; no upstream issue filed here.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: R7 audit links the already-open upstream issue https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1576. Installed SDK 2026.10.24 BulkItemUpdateMutation.match accepts only a metadata key/value; BulkItemCloseMutation has no match or expectedItemHash/expectedHistoryHead. commitWorkspaceTransaction provides a workspace lease but ordinary native writers acquire item leases independently. mutateItemWithHistoryContext permits history reads inside its callback, but cannot compose a native lifecycle update under that same non-reentrant item lease. The internal runWithItemMutationPrecondition callback is synchronous and not a public SDK export. A beforeMutation hook can inspect history under the native item lease; SDK setActiveExtensionHooks replaces the full registry and offers no public additive scoped guard or registry snapshot. Disabling extensions as in a hook workaround would bypass existing policy/hooks and lose extension-owned runtime schema; hand-applying native update/close/hierarchy behavior would violate SDK adoption. Required public contract: native lifecycle/bulk expectedHistoryHead (length plus record hash), or expectedItemHash, checked under the existing item lease; alternatively an additive request-scoped transactional guard that preserves the active extension runtime. Native sync update sites and resolution agreement publication remain blocked on this contract; not marked fixed. A package-level fixed-clock boundary probe is being captured in disposable source copies with the real SDK.
